round1.ci: Tests runs 34748320522 and 34748371374 at 431a0d7a82922dcbda249634263e1619c7fca892: lint, pr-title, typecheck, test all success (gh pr checks 1010; check-runs API). No job named pr-checks-result exists on this workflow.
observations: FINDING for the architect/implementer (rig coexistence, adjacent to this change): the daemon also binds worker_stream_port = LEGION_DAEMON_PORT + 1 (default), but up.sh asserts only LEGION_DAEMON_PORT is free (assert_port_free 'Legion daemon' "$daemon_port") and the README's 'Two rigs share one machine when each has its own SMOKE_PROJECT, SMOKE_DIR, and ports' does not mention the neighbour port. First attempt used daemon ports 19381 (rig A) and 19382 (rig B): rig B came up, rig A's daemon died at boot — daemon.log: 'error: worker_stream_port 19382 on 127.0.0.1 is unavailable: Failed to listen at 127.0.0.1' (EADDRINUSE) — and up.sh reported 'error: Legion daemon exited; inspect /tmp/legion-smoke-41'. Suggested fix in this PR: assert_port_free 'Legion worker stream' "$((daemon_port + 1))" in up.sh main() and one README sentence saying the daemon binds LEGION_DAEMON_PORT+1 too (so two rigs need daemon ports at least 2 apart). Recorded in the PR body's E2E section as a tester finding.

Pre-existing, unrelated to this PR: both rig daemons logged '[legion] failed to connect controller shim socket on ready: … Worker RPC "negotiate_protocol" timed out after 5000ms' right after /controller/ready; the controller pane stayed alive, its role claim was recorded, and the tmux window was live. Not a container-name defect; noted for whoever owns the controller RPC path.

Pre-existing quirk in down.sh (untouched by this PR): terminate_pid_file prints 'STOPPED <name>' only when the process needed SIGKILL; a daemon or listener that exits promptly on SIGTERM is stopped silently. Teardown output therefore shows only the tmux-session and NATS lines.

During the first attempt's teardown (08:49Z) another tester's rig container with the OLD fixed name legion-smoke-nats (port 14222, from a pre-PR up.sh) was live on this machine; my two down.sh runs removed only legion-smoke-nats-sjawhar41 and legion-smoke-nats-sjawhar42 and left legion-smoke-nats listed — incidental real-world confirmation that a record-bearing rig's teardown never touches the fixed-name container.

SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE=none was used (envoy mode would bridge production events and admit real work into the rigs; the criterion is coexistence). Under none, checkpoint 1 is SKIPPED-BLOCKED by design, so the controller-alive check was made directly against daemon state and the private tmux server, exactly as checkpoint_one's controller half does.

Environment scrub: the launcher removed every LEGION_* variable and DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE from this worker pane's environment before exec'ing up.sh, so neither rig daemon inherited this pane's LEGION_OMP_PATH, LEGION_DAEMON_URL, or role identity. Secrets came only from the `secrets` wrapper and ~/.config/opencode/envoy.json's dispatch.token, never printed.

Cleanup: both rigs torn down; no legion-smoke-nats* container remains; scratch /tmp/legion-smoke-negctl, /tmp/legion41-rig.sh, /tmp/legion41-wait-controller.sh, /tmp/legion-smoke-41 and /tmp/legion-smoke-42 removed after the handoff was written. Two disposable root issues remain in LEGSMOKE (LEGSMOKE-108, LEGSMOKE-109), per the rig's documented intent.
